description.value: The study examined resting-state functional connectivity of bilateral habenula regions in autistic and neurotypical individuals, including diagnostic group differences, age-related developmental variability, and associations with autism-related phenotypic measures.

design.value: A multisite, cross-sectional resting-state functional MRI study using participants from the ABIDE I and II datasets. Participant-level habenula-to-whole-brain correlation maps were compared between autism spectrum disorder and neurotypical groups, modeled as a function of age and phenotypic measures while controlling for sex and scanning site.

name.value: Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS) Social Motivation subscale

description.value: The 11-item Social Motivation subscale measured the extent to which an individual is generally motivated to engage in social-interpersonal behavior.

name.value: Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS) Social Communication subscale

description.value: The 22-item Social Communication subscale measured reciprocal and expressive communication in social situations.

name.value: Behavior Rating Inventory of Executive Function (BRIEF) Global Executive Composite Score (GEC) T-score

description.value: The BRIEF GEC T-score measured executive function by compiling scores from composite indexes testing behavior regulation, emotional recognition, and cognitive regulation.
The DLS domain measured adaptive behavior encompassing everyday tasks necessary for independent living, including personal care, household responsibilities, and community activities.

task_description.value: Resting-state functional MRI data were acquired and used to calculate bilateral habenula whole-brain functional connectivity.

description.value: Resting state, functional, and structural MRI data were acquired across the 24 scanning sites using 3T MRI scanners. Acquisition parameters were site-specific and full details were available from the ABIDE website.
For all participants, a T1-weighted structural image was collected and used for registration to Montreal Neurological Institute space.

Data were preprocessed using fMRIPrep 23.1.3. Anatomical images were intensity-corrected, skull-stripped, segmented, and spatially normalized to MNI152 space. Preprocessed data underwent manual and automated quality control; participants with a fail rating, excessive head motion, or fewer than 100 usable time points were removed.

steps.value: Removal for framewise displacement greater than 0.35 mm
Removal when fewer than 100 usable time points remained after motion censoring
Denoising using AFNI’s 3dTproject with linear regression of nuisance time series from each voxel

description.value: Bilateral habenula ROIs were manually defined on the ICBM152 template using Mango Image Viewer and dilated by 2 mm in each direction.

steps.value: Manual bilateral habenula delineation following Lawson et al.
Dilation of the resultant ROI by 2 mm in each direction

model_settings.value: Averaged left and right habenula ROI time series were entered into a general linear model to generate whole-brain correlation maps for each participant; correlation maps were Fisher r-to-z transformed.
Group-level regression models included diagnosis as a categorical factor and age as a continuous factor, controlling for sex and scanning site.
Participants aged 5–21 years were analyzed for age-by-group interactions, controlling for sex and scanning site.

Phenotypic main effects among ASD participants and phenotypic interactions between ASD and NT groups were tested using group as a categorical factor and age as a continuous factor, controlling for sex and scanning site. Benjamini-Hochberg correction controlled the false discovery rate.
